name: any argument starting with a digit is taken for a version
catches: refuses --version without a version like 1.2.3

name: the newest release is not said to be the latest
catches: takes the newest release from where releases/latest redirects, and says so first

name: the tag's v is kept, so the latest is never a version
catches: takes the newest release from where releases/latest redirects, and says so first

name: the redirect is not read through wget
catches: resolves the latest through wget when there is no curl

name: a page at releases/latest is read as a redirect to nothing and taken
catches: refuses a releases/latest that does not redirect to a tag

edits.from: is_version "${found}" || die "could not tell the latest release from ${url}: it did not redirect to a tag like v1.2.3"

name: a release that is already there is fetched again
catches: fetches a release once and reuses it

name: the installer is handed nothing but --source
catches: passes every other argument through unchanged

name: the installer is not told where its release is
catches: hands the installer its own release directory as --source

name: a release without install.sh is put in place and handed over to
catches: refuses a release without install.sh, and leaves nothing behind

edits.from: [ -f "${work}/unpacked/install.sh" ] || die "release ${version} has no install.sh; there is nothing to hand over to"

name: a fetch that fails leaves its working directory behind
catches: refuses a release without install.sh, and leaves nothing behind

name: a 404 is downloaded as if it were the archive
catches: refuses a download that fails, in one line

name: a release directory without install.sh is reused
catches: refuses a release directory that is there without install.sh

edits.from: [ -f "${target}/install.sh" ] || die "${target} is there but has no install.sh; remove the directory and run this again"

name: any operating system is taken for Linux
catches: refuses anything but Linux in one line

edits.from: [ "${system}" = "Linux" ] || die "only Linux is supported, and this is ${system}"

name: tar is not looked for before the download
catches: refuses to run without tar

edits.from: command -v tar >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "tar is required to unpack a release, and it is not on your PATH"

name: curl and wget are not looked for before the download
catches: refuses to run without curl or wget

edits.from:
command -v curl >/dev/null 2>&1 || command -v wget >/dev/null 2>&1 ||
        die "curl or wget is required to download a release, and neither is on your PATH"

name: the question is asked with no terminal to ask on
catches: asks nothing when there is no terminal, or when anything was said

name: the question is never asked
catches: asks which version when nothing was said and there is a terminal to ask on

name: an empty answer is refused rather than taken as the latest
catches: takes an empty answer as the latest

name: the copy is not made runnable
catches: installs itself, links it into ~/.local/bin, and says how to put that on the PATH

name: the copy is not linked into ~/.local/bin
catches: runs from its place once installed

name: the PATH line is printed whether or not ~/.local/bin is on it
catches: says nothing about the PATH when ~/.local/bin is on it

name: the copy goes under ~/.local/share whatever XDG_DATA_HOME says
catches: keeps the copy under $XDG_DATA_HOME when the variable is set

name: whatever the address serves is installed as the command
catches: refuses a copy that is not this script, and installs nothing

edits.from: grep -qF -- "${marker}" "${work}" || die "could not fetch openovai from ${self_url}"

name: a piped run is taken for a run from its place
catches: installs itself through every sh on this machine alike

name: a terminal with no script at $0 installs the command rather than refusing
catches: refuses a terminal with no script at $0, in one line

edits.from:
elif [ -t 0 ]; then
    die "run this from a pipe (curl -fsSL ${self_url} | sh) or from where it is installed"
